content: Emetrol is the brand name of an over-the-counter antiemetic medication that is used to alleviate nausea and vomiting. It is composed of glucose, fructose, and phosphoric acid, and is available in syrup form. Each dose contains 5 mg of phosphoric acid. The inactive ingredients in Emetrol include FD&C Red No. 40, flavoring agents, glycerin, methylparaben, and purified water. Due to the presence of fructose in its formulation, Emetrol should not be taken by individuals with hereditary fructose intolerance (HFI). Patients with diabetes are advised to consult their physician before using this medication. According to the manufacturer, Pfizer, Emetrol should not be used for more than one hour (or more than five doses) without consulting a physician. If symptoms of an upset stomach persist or occur frequently, it is recommended to seek medical advice from a healthcare professional. For optimal effectiveness, the medication should not be diluted, and no fluids of any kind should be consumed immediately before or after taking it.
